text:
The loudest conversation around the Lightning this week was about Nikita Kucherov's future, with Elliotte Friedman's reporting on a possible Montreal plan setting off a wave of Canadiens rumors. Nothing has happened, and the more pressing story is closer to home: Tampa Bay has lost three straight, outscored 15-5, and the injuries are stacking up.

Conor Geekie is out four to five months after shoulder surgery (NHL.com), and Pontus Holmberg is out a month, per Daily Faceoff. That second one stings more than it sounds. Holmberg's line with Zemgus Girgensons and Ilya Mikheyev has been Jon Cooper's best checking unit, 56% of the expected goals and an 11-5 goal edge. Brandon Hagel is back from injured reserve, at least.

Over the full season, this is still one of the East's best teams: 15-8-2, 54% of the expected goals, 55% at five on five. Kucherov, Jake Guentzel and Brayden Point have outscored opponents 11-4, and both top pairs are excellent, John Carlson with Charle-Edouard D'Astous at 63% of the expected goals and Ryan McDonagh with Erik Cernak at 59%. Cernak has 8 points in his last 10 on 3.2 expected, which will not last.

The worry is in net. Dennis Hildeby is .843 over his last five starts, 5.1 goals worse than expected, and the losing streak has been partly earned (47% of the expected goals). Our numbers still give Tampa Bay a 92% chance at the playoffs. What we'd watch: who stops pucks over the next two weeks.
